scientific_rationale: Frozen confirmation of the R15_v2 pointwise local-assignment coordinate reward on region F_b011_s030__reference. The hypothesis is bound to the implemented pointwise operator (local Hungarian assignment, robust per-point distance to observed teacher coordinates, units A) with no chemical-role or energy assumption; the assignment_element_cost term is a detached correspondence cost, not a direct elemental force. The measured current-program response (parent/response) is a bounded, non-clipping displacement field: 40 active and 40 nonzero updates, injected_rms_A_mean 0.0299 A, atom_clip_fraction and cumulative_clip_fraction 0.0, dose_gain_mean 1.0, assignment_switch_fraction mean 0.0167. The confirmation question is whether this same frozen numerical function, run on the configured larger/new prior pool against a matched unguided pool sharing saved priors, random streams, checkpoint and native protocol, retains its measured execution response and yields a terminal tail-utility difference. Formation of the local observable is a mechanism check, not terminal success. Parent-pool outcomes (U_tau 0.0189, best_qualified_pic50 8.5888, mean_all_pic50 7.8421, hit_fraction 0.0417, n_above_target 0, n_qualified 23 of 24 scored) are parent-pool results and are not a forecast for the new pool. Prior rounds are heterogeneous interventions on a reused prior pool, not independent replicates or isolated operator effects; the pointwise family shows 10 of 11 conditions with lower tail than reference, and R15_v2 assignment_element_cost is the one pointwise condition with a positive tail delta (+0.00645) and mean delta (+0.01457) versus reference. These are descriptive same-restored-state comparisons and do not establish a universal operator effect.
